src/business/logic/GateLog.ts: `constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService)` injects the ORM client directly
src/business/logic/GateLog.ts:7 `await this.prisma.scan.create({ data: { id: `${gate}:${code}`, code, gate, at: new Date() } })` writes through Prisma directly
src/business/logic/GateLog.ts:12 `this.prisma.scan.findMany()` reads raw rows through Prisma and aggregates them with no domain type

src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: `new Event(data.id, data.title, data.venueCapacity, data.seatsSold, data.startsAt, data.priceCents)` in purchase() is repeated as `new Event(d.id, d.title, ...)` in listing()
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module handles one concern, ticketing: BoxOffice covers purchase, admission and listing, and GateLog records gate scans. That concern holds together. The problem is how the module reaches persistence. BoxOffice goes through the persistence ports EventStore and TicketStore, loads rows and rebuilds domain objects (Event, Ticket) before applying rules. GateLog skips that store/port approach. It injects PrismaService and calls the ORM client directly, using `this.prisma.scan.create` and `this.prisma.scan.findMany`. It also works on raw rows with no domain type in between. Both candidate flags hold up against the source. So the two files use different persistence abstractions, and GateLog bypasses the store pattern the module follows elsewhere. That fails the rubric's consistent-abstraction and persistence-through-port criteria. A smaller point: the row-to-Event mapping (`new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)`) is copied in both purchase() and listing() in BoxOffice.ts. That is repeated reconstruction logic, not a shared definition. It is minor next to the persistence bypass.

violations.message: GateLog uses the ORM client (PrismaService: prisma.scan.create and prisma.scan.findMany) directly, skipping the module's store/port abstraction. Its sibling BoxOffice reaches persistence only through the EventStore and TicketStore ports. Scan persistence should go through a matching store port, and GateLog should work with a domain type rather than raw rows.

The row-to-Event reconstruction (`new Event(id, title, venueCapacity, seatsSold, startsAt, priceCents)`) is written out twice, in purchase() and in listing(), instead of one shared mapping definition. This is minor.
